ig_carousel_topic.topic: Bankroll math for people who've never thought about bankroll
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Most bettors lose not because they pick wrong.
They lose because they size wrong.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common approach: bet whatever feels right.
$50 here, $200 when confident, $20 when nervous.
No structure. No floor. No ceiling.
That's not betting, that's guessing with extra steps.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Flat betting fixes this.
Pick a unit size: 1% to 2% of your total bankroll per bet.
At $1,000 that's $10 to $20 per play.
Now a losing streak hurts less and a winning streak compounds cleanly.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: $500 bankroll, 1% unit = $5/bet.
You go 54-46 over 100 bets at -110 odds.
Flat betting: net roughly +$18 on the season.
Random sizing at 2x-5x on 'confident' plays: easily -$80 or worse on the same record.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
A 54% win rate at -110 is genuinely profitable.
Bad sizing turns that same record into a net loss.
The math isn't complicated. Most people just skip it.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Sizing kills more bankrolls than bad picks do. The math behind flat betting is simple and most people ignore it.
